claim: Passage is a Sanskrit dharani for protection or realization
evidence: Generic description of a transliterated mantra; no specific fact.

claim: The mantra is the Sanskrit dharani of Ushnishavijaya in Tibetan phonetics
evidence: Ushnishavijaya Dharani text taught by Amitayus; short mantra Om Bhrum Svaha / Om Amrita Ayurdade Svaha matches the passage, which is followed by a praise of Ushnishavijaya.

claim: Om Sarva Tathagata Anuraga Vajra Svabhava Atmako Aham = 'I am the nature of the Vajra that is the passion of all Tathagatas'
evidence: The mantra appears in Kalachakra sadhana, rendered 'all Tathagatas' attachment/passion, vajra is my self-nature'; anuraga=passion, svabhava=nature.

claim: Pema Lingpa lived 1450-1521
evidence: Pema Lingpa (March/April 1450 - February 1521).

claim: Pema Lingpa was a famous Bhutanese treasure revealer (terton)
evidence: Bhutanese saint, 'preeminent tertön', born in Tang valley, Bumthang; matches the passage's 'born in Mon Bumthang'.

claim: skye mched drug = Sanskrit shadayatana (six sense bases)
evidence: 84000 glossary: six sense bases, Skt ṣaḍāyatana, Tib. skye mched drug.

claim: 'Bhadanta' refers to Srilata
evidence: Srilata is a Sautrantika associated with Vasubandhu, but I found no source tying THIS Bhadanta passage (form/sound/touch in dhyanas) to him; 'Bhadanta' in the Kosa is used for several figures (e.g. Dharmatrata, Ghosaka).

claim: Srilata was a Sautrantika teacher
evidence: Srilata is a famous Sautrantika, author of the Sautrantika-vibhasa, teacher of Vasubandhu per search summary.

claim: thams cad shes pa nyid = sarvajnata (omniscience)
evidence: 84000 glossary equates sarvajñatā with thams cad mkhyen pa (nyid); 'thams cad shes pa nyid' is not the standard rendering, though the Sanskrit and meaning are right.
correction: Standard Tibetan: thams cad mkhyen pa nyid (Skt sarvajñatā)

claim: Note text is mis-segmented passage prose; embedded gloss 'amrita' for nectar
evidence: No isolated factual claim; 'amrita' as Sanskrit for nectar is standard.

claim: Rinchen Zangpo lived 958-1055
evidence: Rinchen Zangpo (958-1055), Great Translator of Guge (search hit and Treasury of Lives entry).

claim: Rinchen Zangpo was a key figure in the later dissemination (Second Propagation) of Buddhism in Tibet
evidence: Responsible for many translations of the texts of the Second Propagation under the Guge kings.

claim: The yogi is Milarepa, 11th-century yogi
evidence: Milarepa lived 1052-1135 (11th-12th c.), but the passage only says 'the yogi' with no name, so the identification is not decidable from context.

claim: Milarepa was the principal disciple of Gampopa
evidence: Relationship is reversed: Gampopa was Milarepa's foremost disciple.
correction: Gampopa was the principal disciple of Milarepa, not the other way round.

claim: 'Lord of Dharma Gyare' = Tsangpa Gyare
evidence: Tsangpa Gyare Yeshe Dorje (1161-1211), known as Gyalwa/Je Gyare.

claim: Tsangpa Gyare founded the Drukpa Kagyu
evidence: Drukpa Kagyu was founded in the 12th century by Tsangpa Gyare.

claim: Four means of gathering disciples: generosity, pleasant speech, purposeful activity, consistency
evidence: Samgrahavastu: dana, priyavadita, arthacarya, samanarthata (84000 glossary / Encyclopedia of Buddhism).

claim: Note text (secret chakra / Mother channel)
evidence: Extracted note is a long run of passage prose rather than a discrete claim.

claim: Cool Grove = Shitavana (charnel ground)
evidence: Sitavana = bsil ba tshal, Cool Grove, one of the eight great charnel grounds.

claim: 'Yaksha' in 'Brought by the Yaksha' refers to the divine power of Shakra
evidence: Parallel Mahavastu account has Shakra provide the washing stone (via the Four Great Kings); the passage itself says Shakra brought it, so the reading fits, but no source found for the epithet 'yaksha' meaning Shakra.

claim: mer-mer-po stage is the second week of embryonic development
evidence: Embryo stages: kalala (nur nur po) week 1, arbuda (mer mer po) week 2 per Tibetan embryology sources (tibetanmedicine-edu.org).

claim: Maudgalyayana: one of the Buddha's closest disciples, known for miraculous powers
evidence: Chief disciple with Sariputra, foremost in supranormal powers (rddhi); context names him.

claim: Lantsa is a formal Sanskrit-derived script used for mantras
evidence: Ranjana, in Tibetan 'lantsa', is a decorative script for Sanskrit mantras and dharanis.

claim: Visual description of mandala (eight-petaled lotus, skulls)
evidence: Image description of the page, not a checkable external fact.

claim: snying rje chen po = Sanskrit mahakaruna (great compassion)
evidence: 84000 glossary: snying rje chen po = mahākaruṇā, great compassion.

claim: Passage is a Sanskrit mantra preserved in Tibetan text
evidence: Descriptive of the passage; no specific identification made.

claim: The sequence is the complete Tibetan alphabet in order
evidence: Tibetan has 30 consonants in standard order ka kha ga nga ... ha a; the passage's 30-letter list matches.
